title: Restructure Callaway chart editor into a 13x5 gross-score grid with per-column adjustments and 0.5 worst-hole increments

requirements.text: Update the Admin Callaway chart editor UI to use a fixed grid layout of 13 rows by 5 columns for gross-score chart entry, replacing the current variable-length row list table.

quotes: format the chart editor to have 13 rows and 5 columns for gross scores

acceptanceCriteria: In the Admin Panel > Callaway Chart Editor, the chart editing surface is a 13 (rows) x 5 (columns) grid for gross-score chart editing.
The previous row-based table UI (Row / Lower Bound / Upper Bound / Worst Holes / Adjustment) is no longer the primary editing format for gross scores.
The grid is rendered for both 18-hole and 9-hole tabs (even if their underlying defaults differ).

requirements.text: For each of the 5 gross-score columns in the chart editor grid, add an 'Adjustment' input row that applies to all gross-score cells in that same column, and ensure this per-column adjustment is saved/loaded alongside the chart data.

quotes: for each column have a row for adjustments that apply to all scores in their corresponding column

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the 5 columns has a clearly labeled Adjustment input that is visually associated with that column (one adjustment value per column).
Changing a column’s adjustment affects the calculated adjustment used for any gross score that maps to that column.
Saving and reloading the chart preserves the per-column adjustments.
Reset-to-defaults restores the default per-column adjustments.

requirements.text: Allow 'worst holes' values in the chart editor to be entered and persisted in increments of 0.5, and update Callaway calculation logic to correctly handle half-hole deductions.

quotes: Allow for worst holes to be entered in increments of 0.5

acceptanceCriteria: The worst-holes input(s) in the chart editor accept values like 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5 (step 0.5) and reject values not on a 0.5 increment.
Chart validation allows non-negative worst-holes values in 0.5 increments.
Callaway deduction calculation correctly handles X.5 worst holes by deducting the sum of the worst X holes plus half of the next-worst hole (based on sorted worst hole scores).
All screens that display calculation results (leaderboard and breakdown) continue to work with fractional worst-hole deductions without crashing or showing NaN.
Backend Callaway calculation (backend/main.mo) is updated to match the same half-hole deduction behavior if backend results are used for ranking/output.

requirements.text: Update chart persistence and loading to be backward compatible with any previously saved row-based edited charts in localStorage, so the app can still load without errors after this chart format change.

quotes: format the chart editor to have 13 rows and 5 columns...

acceptanceCriteria: If old edited chart data exists in localStorage (saved by the previous row-based format), the app does not crash on Admin screen load.
The persistence layer either (a) migrates old stored data into the new 13x5 + per-column adjustments representation, or (b) safely ignores invalid/legacy data and falls back to defaults.
Save and Reset actions continue to work after the change.

constraints: Do not modify any files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or frontend/src/components/ui (compose existing UI components instead).
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo; only add backend/migration.mo if state upgrade is strictly required.
nonGoals: Do not add new authentication providers (only existing Internet Identity flow).
Do not add real-time sync or multi-user collaboration for chart editing.
Do not introduce external databases or non-local persistence for the chart editor.
